svg.title: The Operator Desk Facing the Permit and Docket Clock
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-regulatory-permit-desk; chapter number: 11; title: The Operator Desk Facing the Permit and Docket Clock; subtitle: Bonding, testimony, gas composition and facilities around one regulatory lead; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Regulatory and permitting lead; headcount: Not specified in testimony; focus: The permit and the docket clock control the money. Operator witnesses ask for roughly 90-day windows rather than 30.; spokes: role: Bonding analyst; type: Financial assurance; kpi: Marginal and inactive share checked against the 15% trigger before signing; McGowan's 100-well example hit $15 million overnight; role: Hearing witness and exhibit reviewer; type: Docket testimony; kpi: Redline reconciled with direct testimony and every exhibit cost line audited; Devon had to explain $1.27 million that was really the $1.3 million credit; role: Gas composition engineer; type: Takeaway compliance; kpi: Sour gas checked against the 10,000 ppm takeaway limit; Devon faced roughly 13,500 ppm; role: Facilities planner; type: Surface infrastructure; kpi: About $350,000 avoided by tying new horizontals into existing facilities; caption: Tiered blanket bonds run from $150,000 for 1-5 wells up to $1 million for 26-plus wells, while public commenters put average plugging at $163,000.; assumptions note: The roles are an organizing frame for the testified gates, not a staffing plan any speaker described. Every number is quoted from hearing testimony or operator statements.; note: Attributed to New Mexico Oil Conservation Commission hearings (gfqoliQ78bk, -7pNwWErBfk), OCD Pecos Hall (Gyi9ijeMNgA) and Alpha Seven Energy (gjm7ZmMazmc) on YouTube.
